resolutions.title: Scenario count drift across tasks.md + design.md + spec.md (real count = 10)
resolutions.decision: reconcile both downstream artifacts to the spec's actual count: 8 net-new = 1 happy path + 7 edge cases on top of 2 existing baseline = 10 total
resolutions.action: Updated tasks.md L55 (task 3.3): replaced '7 new scenarios covering happy path + 6 edge cases' with '8 net-new scenarios = 1 happy path + 7 edge cases on top of the 2 existing baseline scenarios = 10 scenarios total'. Updated design.md L105: replaced '6+ new scenarios cover happy path + 5 edge cases' with '8 net-new scenarios cover the happy path (1) + 7 edge cases (markers-found-precedence / no-candidates / explicit --from-file override / multiple candidates with recency tie-break / standard ingest lifecycle / --mark no-longer-prerequisite / archive-location respected)' — also enumerated the 7 edge cases for clarity.

resolutions.title: Markers-precede-discovery rule implicit in spec; needs explicit MUST
resolutions.decision: codify the priority order normatively in the MODIFIED requirement intro
resolutions.action: Added TWO normative paragraphs to spec.md MODIFIED requirement intro (around L5): (1) 'Discovery priority order (normative)' block enumerating the 3-step priority: markers grep first → JSON discovery → clean exit, with explicit notes that --from-file always overrides regardless of state; (2) 'Positional argument resolution (normative)' block specifying the change-name-recognition rule (resolves to openspec/changes/<name>/ or archive/<date>-<name>/), which doubles as the fix for SUGG 2.

resolutions.title: TS collision tie-break unspecified
resolutions.decision: specify deterministic tie-break in the 'Multiple JSON candidates' scenario
resolutions.action: Extended spec.md 'Multiple JSON candidates resolved by recency' scenario with: 'If two candidate files share an identical <TS> token (rare; possible only if emitted within the same ISO-second), tie-break by stable lexicographic sort of the full filename (e.g., audit-drift-<TS>.json sorts before review-proposal-<TS>.json before review-system-<TS>.json) and the alphabetically-earlier filename wins.' Worked alphabetical-order example included for codegen-clarity.

resolutions.title: Path-vs-change-name disambiguation rule unspecified
resolutions.decision: specify the recognition rule in the MODIFIED requirement intro
resolutions.action: Combined into the WARN 2 fix above — the new 'Positional argument resolution (normative)' block at spec.md L5 area specifies: 'a positional argument is treated as a change name if and only if it resolves to a directory at openspec/changes/<name>/ OR openspec/changes/archive/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<name>/. Otherwise the positional is treated as a path/pattern scope for the grep, and auto-discovery does NOT apply.' This rule applies normatively to both the 'Scoped scan' scenario and the 4 change-name-positional scenarios.

resolutions.title: Task 2.4 enum extension misses the field-note prose at L69
resolutions.decision: broaden task 2.4 to require BOTH JSON-shape enum + field-note prose updates
resolutions.action: Updated tasks.md L42 (task 2.4) to explicitly require updates at BOTH sites: (a) the JSON-shape enum at run-summary-schema.md L31 (extend `whole-repo | scope | from-file` to include `auto-discovered`); AND (b) the field-note prose at L69 (currently only describes the three existing values — extend to describe auto-discovered and when it's used). Added a drift-risk note: 'mismatched enum vs prose is a drift risk caught by future audit-drift Cat 3'.
